story: Anchorage Neighborhood Health Center, an Anchorage FQHC that already runs an ambient AI scribe but whose patient front door is still one phone number and a 1 to 2 business day callback loop

contact.notes: Re-fetched both pages independently of the researcher. The address is present on both, in two different sentences. No named-leader direct address exists on any page fetched. Nothing was pattern-guessed.

claims.claim: ANHC publishes executiveassistant@anhc.org as the way to reach a member of its leadership team.
claims.verbatim: To contact a member of ANHC's leadership team, please send an email to executiveassistant@anhc.org or call 907-743-7368.
claims.notes: Re-fetched. Exact string confirmed on the live page. This is the intended contact and it clears.

claims.claim: The same address appears again on ANHC's board of directors page as the Executive Assistant and Board Liaison.
claims.verbatim: please contact the ANHC Executive Assistant and Board Liaison at executiveassistant@anhc.org or call 907-743-7368.
claims.notes: Independent corroboration on a second ANHC page. The role title confirms the contact is a ROUTER to leadership and the board, not a decision maker. Anything written to it must survive a forward.

claims.claim: ANHC lists 907-743-7368 as the leadership phone line, separate from the main patient line.
claims.verbatim: please send an email to executiveassistant@anhc.org or call 907-743-7368.
claims.notes: Same sentence as C01.

claims.claim: Lisa DH Aquino is ANHC's Chief Executive Officer.
claims.verbatim: Lisa DH Aquino, MHS
claims.notes: Listed with the title Chief Executive Officer on the live leadership page.

claims.claim: Casey Gokey, MD is ANHC's Chief Medical Officer.
claims.verbatim: Casey Gokey, MD
claims.notes: Matters because the AI scribe quotes downstream are his.

claims.claim: Randee Shafer, LCSW is ANHC's Chief Operations Officer.
claims.verbatim: Randee Shafer, LCSW
claims.notes: Seven C-suite seats are listed. The claim that two were filled in January 2026 was NOT re-fetched and is not carried.

claims.claim: ANHC states on its own about page that it is a Federally Qualified Health Center.
claims.verbatim: Anchorage Neighborhood Health Center is a Federally Qualified Health Center.
claims.notes: Re-fetched.

claims.claim: ANHC began in 1974 as a handful of clinicians working out of a trailer in Fairview.
claims.verbatim: Anchorage Neighborhood Health Center began in 1974 as a handful of clinicians providing care out of a trailer in Fairview.
claims.notes: Re-fetched verbatim. Consistent with the homepage band figure of 52 years (C25).

claims.claim: ANHC's published mission is to be a trusted partner in every person's wellness regardless of ability to pay.
claims.verbatim: To be a trusted partner in every person's wellness by providing integrated, compassionate, and high-quality health care, regardless of ability to pay.
claims.notes: Re-fetched verbatim.

claims.claim: A new patient who registers online with ANHC waits 1 to 2 business days to receive a text with links to the intake forms.
claims.verbatim: Within 1-2 business days, you will receive a text with links to complete the following forms
claims.notes: Re-fetched. First half of the intake loop, ANHC's own published process, not an outside characterization.

claims.claim: A new patient at ANHC waits a further 1 to 2 business days to receive a call to schedule the first appointment.
claims.verbatim: Within 1-2 business days, you will receive a call to schedule your first appointment
claims.notes: Re-fetched. With C10 this establishes that first contact does not produce an appointment. DO NOT sum the two windows into a single stated total, the page does not say they are sequential for every path.

claims.claim: ANHC counts anyone not seen by an ANHC provider in the last 36 months as a new patient.
claims.verbatim: If you have not scheduled your first appointment or have not been seen by an ANHC provider in the last 36 months, you are considered a new patient.
claims.notes: Widens the population that hits the intake loop.

claims.claim: ANHC tells new patients their first appointment may last up to 45 minutes.
claims.verbatim: Your first appointment may last up to 45 minutes.
claims.notes: Re-fetched.

claims.claim: ANHC routes general patient questions, prescription refills and lab results through one main line, 907-743-7200, which also takes a TEXT ME message.
claims.verbatim: Send TEXT ME to our main line, 907-743-7200, to request refills, get lab results, ask questions, and more.
claims.notes: The stronger framing, that this one number carries nearly the ENTIRE front door including after hours, is NOT supported. See C15 and killed K01. Say what the page says, no more.
claims.suggested_phrasing: one main line carries general questions, refills and lab results

claims.claim: ANHC publishes a separate after hours number, 907-330-3267, for established patients to reach its answering service.
claims.verbatim: Established patients can call 907-330-3267 to reach ANHC's answering service outside of normal business hours
claims.notes: THIS CLAIM EXISTS TO CORRECT THE PACKAGE. The research asserted the main line drops to an answering service after hours. It does not, there is a dedicated after hours line. Any study text saying otherwise is wrong.

claims.claim: An ANHC sliding fee discount is valid for one year with documentation or six months with a self declaration.
claims.verbatim: Your sliding fee discount is only valid for one year (if you submitted documentation) or six months (if you completed a self-declaration).
claims.notes: Re-fetched verbatim. The recurring paperwork cycle claim, and it holds cleanly.

claims.claim: ANHC's temporary self declaration of income discount is valid for 30 days and can only be used once every twelve months.
claims.verbatim: This temporary discount is valid for 30 days. You must provide proof of household income within 30 days to continue to receive the discount.
claims.notes: The once every twelve months limit is on the same page verbatim: 'You may only use the temporary Self-Declaration of Income form once every twelve months.'

claims.claim: ANHC requires a new sliding fee application when a patient is new, after a change in household size or income, and before the discount expires.
claims.verbatim: You should complete a new sliding fee discount application: If you're a new patient at ANHC. After a change in your household size or annual income. Before your discount expires.
claims.notes: Re-fetched. Use this string, the package paraphrased the order.

claims.claim: ANHC publishes its sliding fee application forms in English, Spanish, Tagalog and Samoan.
claims.verbatim: English, Spanish, Tagalog, Samoan
claims.notes: FOUR written languages against the 56 languages claimed as translated on the homepage (C20). That gap is real and is the honest way into the language topic.

claims.claim: ANHC's homepage statistics band claims 56 languages translated.
claims.verbatim: 56 languages translated
claims.notes: Re-fetched verbatim. The band carries NO period label, so this is not a per year figure and must never be printed as one.
claims.suggested_phrasing: ANHC's homepage reports 56 languages translated

claims.claim: ANHC's homepage statistics band shows 47,783 patient visits.
claims.verbatim: 47,783 patient visits
claims.notes: Unlabeled period. See C31 for the reconciliation problem.
claims.suggested_phrasing: the homepage currently shows 47,783 patient visits, with no period stated

claims.claim: ANHC's homepage statistics band shows 7.1 million dollars in uncompensated care.
claims.verbatim: $7.1 million in uncompensated care
claims.notes: Unlabeled period, and the label differs from the 2024 report's 'care provided regardless of ability to pay'. Not a like for like series.
claims.suggested_phrasing: the homepage currently shows $7.1 million in uncompensated care, with no period stated

claims.claim: ANHC's homepage statistics band shows 2,929 health insurance assists.
claims.verbatim: 2,929 health insurance assists
claims.notes: Unlabeled period.

claims.claim: ANHC's homepage statistics band shows 95 percent patient satisfaction.
claims.verbatim: 95% patient satisfaction
claims.notes: Unlabeled period. DO NOT present the move from 95.7 percent to 95 percent as a decline, the two figures are not stated to cover comparable periods.

claims.claim: ANHC's homepage statistics band shows 52 years of service to the community.
claims.verbatim: 52 years of service to our community
claims.notes: Sanity check passes. 1974 plus 52 lands in 2026, consistent with C08.

claims.claim: ANHC discontinued onsite screening mammography services effective June 2nd, 2026.
claims.verbatim: Anchorage Neighborhood Health Center (ANHC) has discontinued onsite screening mammography services effective June 2, 2026.
claims.notes: Re-fetched verbatim from the live homepage notice. ANHC states it remains committed to breast cancer screening through referral and follow up, so DO NOT frame this as ANHC abandoning screening.

claims.claim: ANHC's 2024 annual report reports 53,021 total visits across services.
claims.verbatim: 53,021 total visits across services
claims.notes: Re-fetched. Post dated 2025-06-02, labeled as the 2024 report.

claims.claim: ANHC's 2024 annual report reports 15,203 unique medical and dental patients served.
claims.verbatim: 15,203 unique medical and dental patients served
claims.notes: Sanity check passes. 53,021 visits over 15,203 patients is about 3.5 visits per patient, a normal FQHC ratio.

claims.claim: ANHC's 2024 annual report reports 5.7 million dollars in care provided regardless of ability to pay.
claims.verbatim: $5.7 million in care provided regardless of ability to pay
claims.notes: Different label from the homepage's 'uncompensated care'. Not proven to be the same measure.

claims.claim: ANHC's 2024 annual report reports 2,198 assists with insurance enrollment and 314 mobile clinic visits at shelters across Anchorage.
claims.verbatim: 2,198 assists with insurance enrollment
claims.notes: The 314 mobile clinic visits figure confirmed on the same page verbatim as '314 mobile clinic visits at shelters across Anchorage'.

claims.claim: ANHC's two published visit figures do not reconcile, 53,021 total visits in the 2024 annual report against 47,783 patient visits on the current homepage.
claims.verbatim: 47,783 patient visits
claims.notes: BOTH sides re-fetched. The study MAY state the figures differ. The study MAY NOT state or imply ANHC's volume fell. The homepage band carries no period label and the metric names differ. THE SINGLE HIGHEST RISK SENTENCE in the package for making the organization look worse than the evidence supports.
claims.suggested_phrasing: the two published figures are not labeled with a period and can't be reconciled from public pages, so this is a definitional mismatch and not a measured decline

claims.claim: ANHC's Chief Medical Officer says he used to spend 10 minutes charting after a 20 minute visit and now spends 25 minutes with the patient and five reviewing the note.
claims.verbatim: Before, I'd spend 10 minutes charting after a 20-minute visit. Now I can spend 25 minutes with my patient and five minutes reviewing the note.
claims.notes: CITATION MOVED. On ANHC's own blog the quote is BROKEN by narration and is not continuous. It is continuous and verbatim on the APCA original. Cite APCA, not the ANHC blog. Operator anecdote with no measured before and after, so it may NEVER be used as a metric.
claims.suggested_phrasing: ANHC's Chief Medical Officer told the Alaska Primary Care Association

claims.claim: ANHC's Chief Medical Officer says the AI tool reduces what clinicians call pajama time.
claims.verbatim: It reduces what we call 'pajama time'
claims.notes: Verbatim span deliberately clipped before the en dash that follows on the page, so the quote can be printed under the house no-dash rule. The full sentence continues 'that after-hours charting so many of us have done for years.'

claims.claim: ANHC already runs an ambient AI documentation tool in clinical production and names no vendor for it anywhere public.
claims.verbatim: It reduces what we call 'pajama time'
claims.notes: Both the APCA article and ANHC's own blog were re-fetched and neither names a vendor or product. THE MOST IMPORTANT FACT IN THE PACKAGE FOR TONE. ANHC is NOT behind on clinical AI, it is AHEAD of every Alaska FQHC peer checked. Any framing that treats ANHC as an AI laggard is factually wrong and will read as an insult.

claims.claim: Federal rules and ANHC bylaws require a majority of ANHC board members to be ANHC patients.
claims.verbatim: a majority of Board members be ANHC patients, ensuring the Board reflects the community we serve.
claims.notes: Corroborated on https://www.anhc.org/board verbatim 'a majority of members must be ANHC patients'. A material new system is board visible, so any urgency or scarcity pressure in the outreach reads badly here.

claims.claim: ANHC's board is made up of between 11 and 17 members and meets monthly.
claims.verbatim: ANHC's Board is made up of between 11 and 17 members.
claims.notes: The people-finder said fifteen. The page states a RANGE. Meetings verbatim: 'Board meetings are typically held from 4:00 to 6:00 p.m. on the last Wednesday of each month.'

claims.claim: ANHC board members serve three year terms with a limit of three consecutive terms.
claims.verbatim: Board members are generally elected to serve three-year terms, with a term limit of three consecutive terms.
claims.notes: Re-fetched.

claims.claim: Alaska Public Media reported that Medicaid accounts for 34 percent of revenue at Anchorage Neighborhood Health Clinic.
claims.verbatim: At Anchorage Neighborhood Health Clinic, it's 34%, and the Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium gets about 40% of its income from Medicaid.
claims.notes: Re-fetched, exact string. Authors Rachel Cassandra and Liz Ruskin. The outlet writes 'Health Clinic', not 'Health Center'. News report rather than an ANHC filing, so it must carry the attribution.
claims.suggested_phrasing: Medicaid is reportedly about 34 percent of revenue, according to Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: ANHC reported total revenue of 31,234,658 dollars for the fiscal year ending June 2025.
claims.notes: Re-fetched. ProPublica republishes the IRS Form 990, one step from primary. Filed as 'Anchorage Neighborhood Health', not 'Center'.
claims.suggested_phrasing: per the Form 990 as published by ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer

claims.claim: ANHC reported total expenses of 29,601,126 dollars for the fiscal year ending June 2025.
claims.notes: Sanity check passes. Revenue exceeds expenses by about 1.63M, a roughly 5 percent margin.

claims.claim: ANHC reported total revenue of 28,822,081 dollars and expenses of 26,339,049 dollars for the fiscal year ending June 2024.
claims.notes: Re-fetched alongside the FY2025 row.

claims.claim: ANHC ran a deficit in the fiscal year ending June 2023, with revenue of 23,297,103 dollars against expenses of 25,603,422 dollars.
claims.notes: Three years old and followed by TWO SURPLUS YEARS, so it is history and not a current condition. DO NOT use it to characterize ANHC's present finances.
claims.suggested_phrasing: FY2023 expenses exceeded revenue by about 2.3 million dollars

claims.claim: ANHC's EIN is 92-0047965 and it has held 501(c)(3) status since March 1975.
claims.notes: Ruling year March 1975 confirmed. Sanity check passes against the 1974 founding.

claims.claim: A JAMA study of ambient AI scribe adoption found 13.4 fewer minutes of EHR time.
claims.verbatim: AI scribe adoption was associated with 13.4 (95% CI, 9.1-17.7) fewer minutes of EHR time
claims.notes: First author Lisa S Rotenstein. The abstract does NOT carry 'per 8 scheduled patient hours'. The denominator is NOT verified and must not be printed. Association, not causation.
claims.suggested_phrasing: associated with, in a difference in differences analysis

claims.claim: The same JAMA study found 16.0 fewer minutes of documentation time.
claims.verbatim: 16.0 (95% CI, 13.7-18.3) fewer minutes of documentation time
claims.notes: Same caution as C44 on the missing denominator.

claims.claim: The same JAMA study found 0.49 additional weekly visits delivered.
claims.verbatim: 0.49 (95% CI, 0.17-0.81) additional weekly visits delivered
claims.notes: Half a visit a week. Any ROI model leaning on throughput has to start from this number, not a bigger one.

claims.claim: The same JAMA study found electronic health record time outside work hours did not change significantly.
claims.verbatim: Electronic health record time outside work hours did not change significantly.
claims.notes: THE HONESTY CLAUSE of the whole scribe argument. It must appear anywhere the 13.4 and 16.0 minute figures appear. It cuts directly against ANHC's own CMO anecdote about pajama time in C33, and the study should say so plainly rather than print both and hope nobody notices.

claims.claim: The JAMA ambient scribe study covered 8,581 clinicians of whom 1,809 were AI scribe adopters.
claims.verbatim: The sample comprised 8581 clinicians, including 1809 AI scribe adopters.
claims.notes: Five academic health systems. Transfer to a single site FQHC is an assumption and must be stated as one.

claims.claim: A six system study found self reported clinician burnout fell from 51.9 percent to 38.8 percent after 30 days of ambient AI scribe use.
claims.verbatim: the proportion of participants experiencing burnout decreased significantly from 51.9% to 38.8% (odds ratio, 0.26; 95% CI, 0.13-0.54)
claims.notes: Olson KD et al, JAMA Netw Open. 2025;8(10):e2534976. 263 clinicians across 6 systems. Self report, no randomization, so suggestive rather than causal.
claims.suggested_phrasing: self reported burnout, in a pre and post quality improvement design with no control group

claims.claim: The same six system study found note related cognitive task load improved by 2.64 points and after hours documentation fell by 0.90 hours.
claims.verbatim: note-related cognitive task load (mean [SE] difference, 2.64 [0.13] points)
claims.notes: The 0.90 hours figure confirmed verbatim on the same page. NOTE THE CONFLICT with C47, where objectively measured after hours EHR time did not move. One is self reported, one is log measured. Say so.

claims.claim: A UCSF Health study found ambient scribe adopters generated 1.81 more RVUs per week.
claims.verbatim: Adopters had 1.81 (95% CI, 0.86-2.75) greater RVUs per week
claims.notes: Holmgren AJ et al. 1,565 physicians, 698 adopters, 1,202,734 ambulatory encounters, all confirmed on the page.

claims.claim: The UCSF authors translate that RVU gain to 3,044 dollars per physician per year at 2025 Medicare rates.
claims.verbatim: 1.81 RVUs per week increase translates to $3044 annually per physician, using the 2025 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule
claims.notes: SANITY CHECK AGAINST C54. At 200 to 600 dollars per clinician per month, annual subscription runs 2,400 to 7,200 dollars, so 3,044 dollars of revenue is BREAK EVEN AT BEST and negative at the top of the range. Any ROI model showing ambient scribing paying for itself on throughput alone contradicts its own source.
claims.suggested_phrasing: the authors translate this to about 3,044 dollars per physician per year

claims.claim: The UCSF study found no difference in the proportion of claims with a denial between scribe adopters and non adopters.
claims.verbatim: There was no difference in proportion of claims with a denial
claims.notes: Useful counterweight to the fear that AI notes trigger payer pushback, at least in this cohort.

claims.claim: A JAMA Network Open commentary states most health systems pay ambient AI scribe subscription fees of 200 to 600 dollars per clinician per month.
claims.verbatim: AI scribes remain costly, with most health systems paying subscription fees of $200 to $600 per clinician per month.
claims.notes: UNIT CORRECTION. The package dropped 'per clinician', which understates cost for a multi clinician organization by roughly the size of the clinical staff. Shah SJ and Garcia P. Note the tension with C55.

claims.claim: One named ambient scribe vendor publishes self serve list pricing from 39 dollars to 119 dollars per clinician per month.
claims.notes: Re-fetched. Starter 39, Core 79, Premier 104 annual or 119 monthly, Groups custom. Vendor list price, the honest FLOOR to put beside the 200 to 600 dollar enterprise figure in C54. Naming the spread is more useful to a safety net buyer than either number alone.
claims.suggested_phrasing: one vendor's published list price, which is not the same as a negotiated organizational contract

claims.claim: The same commentary puts the cost of a single departing physician at 500,000 to 1,000,000 dollars in recruitment, onboarding and lost productivity.
claims.verbatim: each departing physician costing an estimated $500 000 to $1 million in recruitment, onboarding, and lost productivity
claims.notes: An ESTIMATE carried in a commentary, not a measured figure, and US wide not Alaska. NEVER present it as ANHC's cost.
claims.suggested_phrasing: estimated at

claims.claim: The same commentary warns that recent downcoding policies by Aetna and Cigna could offset scribe related revenue gains.
claims.verbatim: recent downcoding policies implemented by Aetna and Cigna may signal a coding arms race that could offset these gains
claims.notes: Belongs in any ROI section that uses C52.

claims.claim: A PLOS Digital Health review found AI translation non inferior to human translation for Spanish.
claims.verbatim: AI-based translation was non-inferior to human translation for Spanish
claims.notes: Finding is about WRITTEN pediatric discharge instructions, not live spoken interpretation.

claims.claim: The same review found Russian translation accuracy fell to about 89 percent for GPT-4 and about 80 percent for Google Translate.
claims.verbatim: GPT-4 fell to ~89% and Google to ~80% accuracy
claims.notes: Directly relevant to a clinic claiming 56 languages translated in C20.

claims.claim: The same review reports up to 6 percent of instruction sets contained potentially harmful errors.
claims.verbatim: with up to 6% of instruction sets containing potentially harmful errors
claims.notes: Sits in the SAME SENTENCE as the Russian accuracy figures in C59, so the two must be presented together and not separated.

claims.claim: The same review found back translation retained only 36 to 76 percent of original meaning for certain non European languages.
claims.verbatim: back-translation of AI-mediated translations into English retained only 36-76% of the original meaning for certain non-European languages
claims.notes: Verbatim uses an en dash on the page. Render as 36 to 76 in prose under the house no-dash rule.

claims.claim: The same review concludes professional human interpreters remain essential for complex, emotionally charged or high stakes clinical communication.
claims.verbatim: Professional human interpreters remain essential for complex, emotionally charged, or high-stakes clinical communication.
claims.notes: REPLACES the package's harder claim that the paper declares real time spoken interpretation unsafe. Use this sentence, not the harder one. See killed K09.

claims.claim: A JMIR Medical Informatics study found ambient AI scribes propagated interpreter errors into clinical notes in simulated English and Spanish encounters.
claims.verbatim: In simulated English and Spanish clinical encounters, ambient AI scribes propagated interpreter errors into clinical notes, with patterns varying by speaker role and error type.
claims.notes: PMID 42520279, Rabotin A et al. SIMULATED, not live clinical, encounters, and that qualifier must survive into the study. THE SHARPEST SAFETY CAVEAT available for a clinic that runs an ambient scribe and serves many languages, and the single most useful industry fact in the package for THIS company.
claims.suggested_phrasing: in simulated encounters

claims.claim: CHCF focus groups with California safety net leaders found AI pricing models do not work for the safety net.
claims.verbatim: The pricing models don't work for the safety net,
claims.notes: Attributed on the page to Kara Carter, CHCF senior vice president for strategy and programs. Three focus groups, 45 California safety net leaders, August to October 2024. California, not Alaska, so analogous and not local.

claims.claim: The same CHCF work found community clinics may lack the data scientists on staff needed to implement AI.
claims.verbatim: A community clinic may not have the data scientists on staff needed to implement AI,
claims.notes: Attributed to Stella Tran, senior program investment officer at the CHCF Innovation Fund. The strongest published argument that the INTEGRATION WORK, not the model, is what a safety net buyer is actually buying.

claims.claim: CHAI and NACHC report that 60 percent of all community health centers and 70 percent of rural ones say expenses were a challenge to implementing emerging technologies.
claims.verbatim: 60% of all CHCs and 70% of rural CHCs report that expenses were a challenge to implementing emerging technologies.
claims.source_outlet: CHAI and NACHC, via PR Newswire
claims.notes: The page says 'emerging technologies', NOT AI specifically. The package narrowed it. Use the page's wording.
claims.suggested_phrasing: according to CHAI and NACHC

claims.claim: A survey of 43 US health systems found ambient notes was the only AI category where 100 percent of respondents reported adoption activity.
claims.verbatim: 100% of respondents report adoption activities
claims.source_outlet: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
claims.notes: Fielded fall 2024. Adoption ACTIVITY is not the same as deployment, and the study must not upgrade it.

claims.claim: In the same survey 53 percent reported a high degree of success with AI for clinical documentation while only 19 percent reported high success with imaging.
claims.verbatim: 53% reported a high degree of success with using AI for Clinical Documentation.
claims.source_outlet: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
claims.notes: Imaging figures confirmed on the same page verbatim. The honest reading is that even the best evidenced category succeeds barely half the time.

claims.claim: In the same survey 77 percent named lack of AI tool maturity as the biggest or second biggest barrier to AI deployment.
claims.verbatim: 77% of respondents identified lack of AI tool maturity as the biggest or second-biggest barrier to AI development or deployment.
claims.source_outlet: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
claims.notes: Use the page wording.

claims.claim: OCHIN measured ambient AI generating 15 percent of all clinical notes at Signature Health by January 2026, or 6,942 of 45,565.
claims.verbatim: 15% of all clinical notes, or 6,942 of 45,565
claims.notes: Sanity check passes, 6,942 over 45,565 is 15.2 percent. OCHIN is the EHR collaborative, a third party to the vendors but not to its own member.
claims.suggested_phrasing: OCHIN, the community health center EHR collaborative, reports

claims.claim: OCHIN measured 14 percent less time spent on notes per day at Signature Health, about eight minutes.
claims.verbatim: 14% less time spent on notes per day
claims.notes: Per active user, measured November 2025. Sanity check, about eight minutes a day is roughly half the JAMA figure in C45, the direction you would expect from a community setting.
claims.suggested_phrasing: reportedly about eight minutes a day per active user

claims.claim: OCHIN measured a 6 percent reduction in after hours charting per scheduled day at Signature Health.
claims.verbatim: 6% reduction in after-hours charting per scheduled day
claims.notes: Small, and the only measured after hours movement in the package that is not self reported. Reconcile against C47, which found no significant change at academic scale.

claims.claim: OCHIN's October 2025 evaluation reported a return of about 5 to 5.50 dollars for every 1 dollar invested.
claims.verbatim: about $5 to $5.50 for every $1 invested
claims.notes: NO METHOD IS PUBLISHED. Sits in DIRECT TENSION with C52, where a peer reviewed study of 1.2 million encounters found roughly break even. Do not use both as though they agree, and do NOT build an ROI model on this one. If quoted at all it must be quoted with C52 beside it.
claims.suggested_phrasing: OCHIN reported, without publishing a method, a return of about 5 dollars per dollar invested

claims.claim: Neighborhood Healthcare, a California FQHC, rolled Nabla's ambient AI assistant out to 200 clinicians in April 2025 after a pilot.
claims.verbatim: 200 clinicians
claims.notes: NUMBER CORRECTED. The package said 220. The page says 200. Serves nearly 100,000 patients annually. Trade press interview with the CIO, so operator reported.

claims.claim: Neighborhood Healthcare reports 34,000 notes generated during and after its pilot with 76 percent rated 4 or higher out of 5 and only 2 percent requiring editing.
claims.verbatim: 34,000 notes generated during and after the pilot
claims.notes: The 76 percent and 2 percent figures confirmed verbatim. The package's claimed 4.3 out of 5 average was NOT found and is killed (K07). A 2 percent edit rate is provider self report and implausibly low as a measure of note accuracy, so it must never be printed without that caveat.
claims.suggested_phrasing: provider reported ratings from a pilot, not an audit of note accuracy

claims.claim: Capital Area Health Network reports an AI contact center handling 80 percent of its total patient call volume.
claims.value: 80% of the total patient call volumes
claims.verbatim: 80% of the total patient call volumes
claims.notes: VENDOR PRESS RELEASE. Named customer, 34 provider FQHC in Richmond, named CEO Tracy Causey. No independent audit, no before and after abandonment rate, no cost disclosed. The closest analogue in the package to ANHC's own phone problem, which is exactly why it needs the hardest hedge.
claims.suggested_phrasing: according to a vendor press release quoting the health center's CEO

claims.claim: The same release states Capital Area Health Network handled roughly 450 patient calls a day with hold times of 30 to 45 minutes before deployment.
claims.verbatim: 30-45 minutes
claims.notes: Same vendor release. The baseline is vendor stated and unaudited.
claims.suggested_phrasing: reported by the vendor as roughly 450 calls a day and 30 to 45 minute hold times before deployment

claims.claim: Providence's chief medical officer told Alaska Public Media that Providence uses an AI tool to surface the highest risk inbound patient messages first.
claims.value: suicidal ideation to the top of the inbox
claims.verbatim: Things like suicidal ideation. We need to get that to the top of the inbox.
claims.notes: Re-fetched, exact string. Serene Perkins, CMO of Providence Medical Group, reported by Rachel Cassandra. Operator reported with no published measurement. Providence matters here specifically because ANHC's own patient portal runs on Providence's Epic instance, see C81.

claims.claim: The same article reports Providence created the generative AI patient message tool in 18 days.
claims.verbatim: created new gen AI tool in 18 days
claims.notes: Operator claim carried by the outlet. No independent verification of the build timeline.
claims.suggested_phrasing: reportedly built in 18 days, according to Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: Providence offers new patients real time online appointment self scheduling at its Anchorage Huffman primary care clinic.
claims.verbatim: New patients can schedule online appointments across nearby primary care clinics.
claims.notes: Re-fetched. The page carries a 'See All Open Times' call to action for new patients and directs established patients to MyChart. THE SINGLE SHARPEST VERIFIED CONTRAST with ANHC's 1 to 2 business day callback loop in C10 and C11, and it is the same Anchorage patient on the same day.

claims.claim: ANHC's patient portal runs on an Epic MyChart instance operated for Providence Health and Services Alaska.
claims.verbatim: MyChart licensed from Epic Systems Corporation 1999 - 2026
claims.notes: Re-fetched the destination directly. The login prompt reads 'Log in with your password for Providence Health and Services Alaska'. VERIFIED is the destination and branding. NOT VERIFIED is that this is an Epic Community Connect arrangement, killed at K05. Say what the login page says and stop there.
claims.suggested_phrasing: ANHC's published portal link resolves to an Epic MyChart login operated for Providence Health and Services Alaska

claims.claim: Interior Community Health Center requires online appointments to be made 48 hours in advance and limits online scheduling to established patients.
claims.verbatim: Online appointments must be made 48 hours in advance, and cannot be canceled or rescheduled within 48 hours of the appointment time.
claims.notes: Established patients only. No AI, chatbot or symptom checker on the page.

claims.claim: Southcentral Foundation's primary care page directs patients to a portal to request an appointment and shows no AI tooling.

drift_pattern: The rejections lean in TWO consistent directions and neither is random. FIRST, toward making ANHC look more troubled, more behind and more phone bound than the evidence supports: the invented answering-service quote, the unverifiable Yelp complaint, the visit-count-as-decline framing, and the 'fifteen roles open' framing. Four separate errors, all pushing the same way. SECOND, and pointing the opposite direction, toward making the AI evidence stronger and cheaper than it is: the 220-versus-200 clinicians inflation, the invented 4.3-out-of-5 note rating, the dropped 'per clinician' on the 200-to-600-dollar subscription figure, the hardened PLOS conclusion, and the invented 'per 8 scheduled patient hours' denominator. Read together the package was drifting toward a story where a struggling clinic buys cheap, well-proven AI. THE VERIFIED RECORD SUPPORTS NEITHER HALF. ANHC is financially stable with two surplus years, it already runs an ambient scribe ahead of its Alaska peers, and the best-evidenced AI in its segment is modest, roughly break even on throughput, and unmeasured on after-hours time. The study must be built on that harder reading or it will be wrong in the way that gets caught.
